title: Renewable Energy Resources
subtitle: Merits/Demerits, Obstacles, Prospects & World Energy Status
learningOutcome: By the end of this week, you should be able to evaluate the merits and demerits of renewable energy, explain obstacles to implementation, and describe world fossil fuel reserves.

content.text: It includes both direct and indirect solar radiation. The direct solar radiation include interception by collectors e.g, solar and flat plate thermal cell. In the indirect solar energy wind, ocean hydropower and biomass are included. The biomass resources can be managed in the sustainable manner. Geothermal technologies have a finit life but considered as renewable for planning purpose. Traditional methods of using biomass and its derivatives viz, wood, and charcoal are highly insufficient in contrast with the modern techniques emphasing proper forest management sustained yield fuel, wood plantation and efficient production.

There are three independent primary sources of energy provided to the earth (a) The sun (b) Geothermal forces and (c) Planetary motion in the solar system. In particular, the direct solar radiation represents an enormous resources for a modern technological civilization. However, the human capacity to harness these gigantic natural flow of energy to perform useful work depends largely on the (i) Economic feasibility (b) Technology development and (c) Efficient use.

content.text: The total amount of solar energy absorbed by the earth and its atmosphere in one year (3.8 × 10²⁴ joules) is equivalent to nearly 25 times the amount of energy stored in all the world's reserves of fossil fuels. Unlike capital energy sources renewable can not be exhausted with limitation to the rate they are used. The question of depletion of any particular reservoir faster than its replenition does not arise.

Some of the renewable energy has already taken a lead viz biomass contribute one seventh of all the fuel consumed: Hydro generates one quarter of the world electricity and sun contributes in space heating of all the structure.
Reasons for more attention concentrating on renewable energy technologies are:

items: • Low transmission costs as unit can often be built on or closed to the site where energy is required.
• They can match in scale of need.
• They can deliver energy of the quality of requirement for a specific work.
• They can be introduced quickly in large number with cost lead times (often 15 year or more).
• Rapid planning and construction lower the unit cost and permits planner to respond quickly to changing patterns of demand.
• The diversity of the systems available enhances flexibility and security of supply.

• Unlike other sources of energy the renewable sources also suffers the risks associated with physical and environmental aspects. However, these are relatively modest in comparison with those associated with fossil fuels/nuclear power.

content.text: The annual primary energy consumption of world was 500 EXA joules (equivalent to 138.8 × 10¹² kWh of the energy or average power of 1.5 × 10⁷ MW) fossil fuel use to provide about 90% of this energy and will continue to provide more than 8.80% of the total demand. Approximately 25% of this energy is consumed by transportation sector and remaining 75% by industries, domestic, agriculture and social consumer sectors. The energy demand will be increased by more than 50% in recent year. This growth is forecasted to continue at annual rate of 3.2%.
If the world continues to consume fossil fuel at rate of 2006, the reserves of coal oil and gas may last for 200, 40 and 70 years respectively.
